observation.visible_scene: An outdoor backyard setting. In the left foreground a staircase built from stacked brown cardboard boxes descends toward the right. At the very top left a person's fingers grip the upper end of a chain of shiny metal spheres. The background (green hedge, tree branches, an overturned yellow pot on grass/dirt) is unchanged throughout.
visible_changes: The chain of metal spheres is fed over the edge of the top step and tumbles downward: a leading sphere that sits on the second step's vertical face at t=0.0s moves progressively right and down, bouncing off step faces and treads, until by t=1.33s it has reached the ground level at the bottom of the steps.
Following spheres cascade in sequence, appearing in mid-air between steps and resting momentarily on vertical faces and horizontal treads as the chain pays out.
The hand at the top remains in roughly the same position, holding the chain's upper end, while the chain lengthens downward along the steps.
The cardboard steps, the hand, and the background remain in fixed positions; the only motion is the chain/spheres moving relative to them.
The camera is stationary (background landmarks do not shift), so the observed motion is object motion, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the release was initiated before t=0.0s and whether the hand is actively pulling the chain or merely holding it while gravity feeds the spheres.
The final resting positions of the spheres after the clip ends.
Whether the spheres are linked by an actual ball-chain or are separate objects strung together.
uncertain_details: Individual spheres seen between steps are ambiguous as 'bouncing' versus 'falling' from single-frame samples.
The exact connectivity of the chain (small links visible near the top, but mid-cascade links are not clearly resolved).
Whether some spheres on a vertical face are momentarily at rest or sliding.
